memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "During that long period, the king of Egypt died. The Israelites groaned in their slavery and cried out, and their cry for help because of their slavery went up to God." - Exodus 2:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A long period — decades. A Pharaoh dies, and perhaps for a moment there is hope that things will change. They do not. The slavery continues, and the people groan.

Notice that the text does not say they prayed eloquently. It says they groaned and cried out. This was not polished, theological prayer. It was the raw sound of exhausted people who could not take any more.

And that sound went up to God.

Some of us have stopped praying because we feel we cannot pray properly any more. We have no words left, only tiredness. Take heart. Scripture says the Spirit Himself intercedes for us through wordless groans (Rom 8:26). Heaven understands the language of a groan.

You do not need the right words. You do not need to sound spiritual. If all you can manage today is a cry, God hears it as clearly as any sermon.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I stopped praying because I feel I cannot pray well?
2. What groan do I need to bring honestly to God today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, sometimes I have no words, only weariness. Receive my groaning as prayer, and meet me in it. Amen.
